question: With nothing hand-authored, can the system observe a real defect at verify time, retrieve knowledge for it, roll back the decision that caused it, and re-make that decision correctly using knowledge-supplied parameters?

observed_tickets.observed: a 3-vertex face is present where 3 of its vertices sit on a corner with 3+ converging edges

rationale: Transfer-tested rule: an odd Bevel segment count leaves a triangle where several beveled edges converge; an even count does not. The even-segment value is a property of the technique, not of the scene, so knowledge supplies it while the observed ticket supplies which corner.
technique parameters supplied by knowledge, not the ticket: ['segments']

rollback.reason: defect classifier observed a corner_triangle at verify time; bevel parity is preventive, so the causing decision is rolled back and re-made with knowledge parameters rather than repaired in place

claim_boundary: This proves the observe->classify->retrieve->plan->rollback->redo loop closes for one structurally-decidable defect class on a synthetic cube, with the defect never being committed. It does NOT prove the classifier covers other defect classes, that the vocabulary generalizes, or that any of this improves resemblance to an unfamiliar reference -- that remains unproven and is the next real gap.
